In an early case-report in 11 aspirin-sensitive asthmatic patients, all developed reactions (rhinorrhoea, tight- ness of chest, wheezing, dyspnoea) after taking naproxen in dos- es of 40 to 80 mg.1 More recently, angioedema occurred after a single dose of naproxen in a patient known to be aspirin-sensi- tive.2 Hypersensitivity to individual NSAIDs is believed to be closely linked to the extent to which these drugs inhibit prosta- glandin (see under Aspirin, p.21). There may therefore be a dose threshold below which no detectable symptoms occur. Such an effect has been reported3 in a patient previously stabilised on naproxen for about one year who had a hypersensitivity reaction after a dosage increase.
